flawed_step: Step 3: the required assertion that any two tours differ in at most ceil(n/2) current-tour edges is false.
counterexample: Let n=6 and k=3. Give edges 12,45,13,36,46 weight 0; edges 23,34,56,61 weight 1; edge 25 weight 2; and every remaining edge weight 10. The tour C=(1,2,3,4,5,6,1) has weight 4 and is a 3-Opt local optimum, but O=(1,2,5,4,6,3,1) has weight 2.
assessment_summary:
1. [JUSTIFIED] Begin a proof attempt with an arbitrary k-Opt local optimum C and a globally optimal tour O, where k=ceil(n/2).
2. [JUSTIFIED] If O differs from C in at most k edges of C, local optimality gives w(C)≤w(O); since O is optimal, C is then globally optimal.
3. [NOT JUSTIFIED] The proof would therefore need every pair of tours to differ in at most ceil(n/2) edges. This is false: for n=6, the tours C=(1,2,3,4,5,6,1) and O=(1,2,5,4,6,3,1) share only edges 12 and 45, so replacing C by O removes four edges, while ceil(6/2)=3.
4. [JUSTIFIED] To show this gap cannot be repaired merely by choosing another nearby improving tour, define nonnegative symmetric weights by w(12)=w(45)=w(13)=w(36)=w(46)=0; w(23)=w(34)=w(56)=w(61)=1; w(25)=2; and weight 10 for each remaining edge of K_6.
5. [JUSTIFIED] The current tour C has weight 0+1+1+0+1+1=4.
6. [JUSTIFIED] The tour O has edges 12,25,45,46,36,13 and hence weight 0+2+0+0+0+0=2.
7. [JUSTIFIED] Any tour containing an edge outside C∪O has weight at least 10, so it cannot be a strictly shorter at-most-3-change from C.
8. [JUSTIFIED] A tour contained in C∪O and obtained by r≤3 changes must remove r edges of C and add r edges from {13,25,36,46}; a distinct Hamiltonian cycle cannot arise for r=1.
9. [JUSTIFIED] For r=2, the only Hamiltonian possibility is to add {25,36} and remove {23,56}. It has weight 4. Adding {13,46} while removing {16,34} gives two triangles, and every other chord pair fails the degree-two condition.
10. [JUSTIFIED] For r=3, the only degree-feasible added set is {13,25,46}. The removed C-edges must be one of the two perfect matchings {12,34,56} or {23,45,61}; both resulting Hamiltonian tours have weight 4. Each other three-chord set violates the degree-two condition at some vertex.
11. [JUSTIFIED] Steps 7–10 exhaust all tours obtainable from C by at most three changes, and none is strictly shorter; therefore C is a 3-Opt local optimum.
12. [JUSTIFIED] Since O has weight 2<4, C is not globally optimal. Thus the asserted universal statement is false.
